projects.description: Inspiration Our environment is only getting worse day by day. What's worse is that many of the factors worsening our environment are consumer-sided. Disposing of food waste uses 1/4 of the world's yearly water usage and worsens our climate with its significant greenhouse gas footprint. Composting is a simple and easy solution to help alleviate many of these issues. However, many people don't compost because the bin can get wet and smelly and frankly, that's not something many people want to deal with. Wormin' Time created Worm Bin to disturb the green bin industry and promote composting. What it does Worm Bin is a smart composter, that tracks the humidity and temperature in the bin and relays that information to the user. When the Bin detects that the humidity and/or temperature gets too high for an extended period, it warns the user, telling them to dispose of their compost before it gets wet and smelly. Additionally, it uses a motorized lid so that the user doesn't need to risk getting their hands dirtier when accessing the bin. How we built it Worm Bin was designed utilizing an Arduino Uno. Attached to the Arduino is a Temperature & Humidity, Infrared Sensor and Ultrasonic Sensor. The Ultrasonic Sensor, Infrared Sensor and Temperature & Humidity Sensor are used to send data to the user, indicating how full the box is and the temperature & humidity in the box. Photoresistors are used to open the box. When triggered it activates a motor on the lid, opening it. Challenges we…

projects.tagline: ARMOR is a heart rate monitoring system that will protect patients and aid personnel from future health problems and assists in exercising/personal health to be deployed at locations worldwide.
projects.description: Inspiration ARMOR was born when our original 7-person team split into groups of 5 and 2 — we were the 2 who stayed together. Fortunately, we shared a strong interest in the Super Human track, which kept us motivated to pursue this project. What it does ARMOR is detecting your pulse or heart rate. projects.description:
Ever wanted to play video games, but without a controller or keyboard? Now with the ElectræGlove Pro 9000-1X you can!
Before starting to assemble the hardware, we had to plan out where to place the IMU units
(that collect accelerometer and gyroscope data) to make meaningful gestures. In the end,
we decided to place units on three separate fingers since moving the fingers would give us
more varied data to work with. We also put the time of flight (ToF) sensor (that dictates
when to brake and is activated by putting another hand above the glove) on the top of the
glove hand. All of the wiring (including the microcontroller that processes the IMU data)
is done on the top of the glove as well (which makes for easier connectivity).
Next, we wrote the code that collects the IMU data. Since each IMU is identical, the I2C
address is also identical, so in order to differentiate between each of the three sensors, we
used a mux and wired a different IMU sensor to each channel of the mux, and then with
the Arduino, we collected data from each mux channel separately. We did a similar process
with the ToF sensor. These inputs are used to activate keyboard commands which are sent
to the computer.
The outcome was a working glove that could interface with “wasd” keys which allows us to
play games. The game we decided to feature with this project is Forza Motorsport 8 which

projects.title: Harry Potter Gobstones
projects.description:
Welcome to Harry Potter Gobstones, the magic marble game. Shoot the magic marbles as close to the center "snake pit" as possible, but don't fall in!
The premise of our project was to bring the magic marble game, Gobstones, from Harry Potter to life by using electromagnets controlled by a stepper motor xy system similar to that of a 3D printer. We split our project into 3 main parts: the software, the mechanics, and the hardware. On the software side, we coded an app through python and CMU graphics to create the marble game on-screen. The play style is similar to that of Angry Birds, where you can click, drag, and release to decide your marbles' trajectory. Each player takes turns to shoot their marbles as close to the center "snake pit" as possible without falling in. Marbles that fall in are removed from the board. On the mechanics side, we cut and engraved a game board and 3D printed marbles in the Harry Potter house colors. We assembled our stepper motor system using aluminum rods, gear belts, and 3D-printed parts. On the hardware side, we calibrated the stepper motors and electromagnet accordingly with the game board using Arduino, breadboard circuits, and soldering. However, we ran into issues putting together these three parts into a full, cohesive game. That being said we are able to demonstrate the software and hardware components individually.

projects.description:
Revolutionize LaTeX typesetting with our specialized keyboard,
designed to streamline equation input and minimize keystrokes.
Experience effortless equation rendering, as our keyboard seamlessly translates your inputs into LaTeX code for optimal efficiency.
LaTeX is always hard and unintuitive to typeset. In constrast, entering equations on
TI-nspire and similar graphing calculators is much more straightforward. So, why not build
a keyboard that is only for LaTeX and make typesetting in LaTeX as simple as entering
equations on TI-nspire?
The tasks of our project is 2-fold. There is a hardward component and a software component.
The hardware is a simple 8x8 keyboard that is smaller than an iPhone. It sends data
through the serial port to a PC. The software component is a web UI that receives keyboard
events from the keyboard and renders them into LaTeX in real time. The web UI should
support features including moving the cursor and backspacing.
Details:
The keyboard is a customized PCB integrating 8x8 buttons and connecting the signal wires
to a ESP32 MCU. The ESP32 is purchased externally and plugged into the socket on the
PCB. ESP32 constantly scans for keyboard events using pull-down input GPIOs ports,
and sends the index of the key pressed to the PC using the UART port.

It was deployed using the Kubernetes software "Docker" and incorporated the Solace PubSub+ WebBroker to communicate between a Qualcomm Dragonboard 410c and the WebBroker over WiFi. The Dragonboard acted as an all in one meteorological unit that can observe the environment around it using the Grove temperature and humidifier sensor, as well as a photoresistor. The Dragonboard was also used to communicate its GPS position for planned scalability involving autonomous deployed drones. projects.description: Inspiration As full-time students, we find ourselves often slouched and with our heads bent forward due to working on p-sets all day or looking at a laptop. With these problems prevalent around us, we made it our mission to resolve these matters. What it does RePause is a device aimed at helping you achieve better posture with live alerts throughout your day. This is all done via a custom-length headband that detects the orientation of your neck. With that input, the device outputs a "buzzing" signal to alert you of misalignment and turns off once corrected. Real-time subtle notifications can help people actively correct their posture. Opposed to existing solutions, ours gets the best of both worlds. Two main solutions exist: one based on tension and one based on stick. Tension solutions act as rubber bands and wrap around peoples' backs, forcing correct posture. However, once the person takes off this device, they fall back into poor posture. The device addresses conditions and not root causes. The second type of solution is a sticky device that adheres to one's back, sending alerts to the user's phone. > A swarm of miniature robots that pick up and rearrange colored blocks! Controlled by their overlord—a computer with a camera looking down...who said Big Brother wasn't watching!?
### General Idea
We plan to make a super-basic swarm robotics demo. The field will consist of a large, flat area with 1 inch colored blocks. Several identical robots with wheel encoders and grippers will drive around, picking up the blocks, and taking them to a central location to assemble a structure. If time permits, we want to allow the arm to move vertically so that we can build vertically as well. The robots will get global localization data from a central manager. This manager will have several cameras pointed down onto the scene. Using the cameras, the manager will use computer vision to identify the location of the blocks and the robots themselves (each robot will have some sort of fiducial like an Aruco marker on it). The manager will also act as a global planner; however, each robot will be able to drive to a new pose on its own.
### MVP and stretch goals
`MVP:` One robot can reliably move blocks and create a 2D structure
`Goal 1:` Three robots can work together to create a 2D structure
`Goal 2:` Three robots can work together to create a **3D** structure
`Goal 3:` Improve the path planning so that the robots work in parallel more effectively (less waiting-around for other robots to get out of the way)

projects.title: RoboSign
projects.description:
A robotic hand that depicts certain numbers.
The purpose of our project was to originally display certain signs in American Sign Language (ASL) using speech to sign on the robotic hand in order to bring awareness to and aid the deaf community. We used servo motors to control the fingers, 3D printed fingers and a laser cut wood pieces for the structure of the hand and palm, illusion cord, string and beads to keep the joints of the fingers taut, filament, and breadboarding materials. We implemented a variety of strategies in order to try to achieve our goal such as: using DC motors, potentiometer angle sensors, and regular motor drivers to drive the circuit but ran into issues regarding the motor drivers' capabilities. We settled on using Servo motors themselves to control the fingers at a maximum rotation angle of 180 degrees. In addition to the hardware component of our project, we developed software using Python to convert speech to text and utilized a media pose library. Additionally, we used Arduino IDE to control the motors' functionality and in tandem the control of the robotic hand. Although we were unable to fully integrate our software with our hardware regarding the signs, and were unable to achieve reliable control of the hands based off of our design, we were able to successfully achieve the speech recognition and gain control of the servo motors.

projects.title: SCOTTYCHORD
projects.description:
Battery-powered mini piano. Play a song on a virtual piano and see
it performed on the Scottychord real-time.
The goal of our project was to build a physical piano-like instrument that could play a
song inputted by a user. In order to play the piano, the user presses keys (on laptop) in
order to play notes on a virtual piano UI. The Scottychord then plays the song back with
the same melody and rhythm that was played. The instrument is built with lyre strings
hit by small wooden hammers. These hammers are glued to motors which spin and hit the
strings to make music. Each motor is connected to a relay, and each relay is connected to
a single 9V battery source. The relay trigger is connected to an Arduino MEGA’s digital
output pins. The piano interface is built using pygame and serial. It sends the song to the
Arduino MEGA as a string. MEGA receives the string via USB and runs code that parses
the string and plays the song.
We ended up changing much of our implementation. Previously, we designed and 3Dprinted a mechanism to pluck the lyre strings, taking inspiration from guitar picking and
a harpsichord (the precursor to the modern piano). However, we found out that the
mechanism was too heavy and required too much precision for the motors. We pivoted to a
wooden hammer mechanism to directly hit the strings to produce sound. The relays ended
up being used to control which keys are played and when. The strings were strung across
the top of the instrument similar to a lyre. We us…

projects.title: Skibot
projects.tagline: The Skibot can do anything.
projects.description: Inspiration: We didn’t want to build another robot that just follows a line like it’s locked onto a track. Those work, but they’re kind of boring to watch. We wanted something that felt more alive: a robot that adjusted, reacted, and moved with a bit of personality. The idea came from downhill skiing: the way skiers carve side to side rather than moving straight down. That’s where Team Ski Bot came from. Our goal was to build a robot that doesn’t just follow a path, but skis along it. What it does: Ski Bot is an edge-following robot that sticks to the right side of a track instead of sitting directly on top of it. It uses a TCS3200 color sensor to tell the difference between the colored boundary and the white/cardboard floor. When it detects red or color, it turns right to stay close to the edge. By constantly moving right, the robot naturally zigzags along the boundary. How we built it: We built it through the provided hardware parts and using Arduino software to upload the code onto the Arduino Uni. The Vision: We integrated a TCS3200 color sensor, which we programmed to ignore "visual noise" and focus on the colored path. <div

projects.description: Inspiration In my house, my parents have taken care of my grandparents after my grandfather had a stroke. Neither of my grandparents can drive anymore, but stroke patients are often unaware of their limitations and reach for the keys anyway. What it does With StarKey, you can keep your keys in the hands of only the drivers in the house. It acts as a normal key rack when a driver is in range and locks access to the keys when no drivers are around to give you peace of mind. How we built it We used the Kinoma Create to pair with drivers' phones via Bluetooth when in range. This actuates the servos on the key rack to unlock access to the keys. We designed AutoDesk Fusion 360 to design our laser-cut hardware pieces. After a lot of filing and elbow grease, we got our StarKey. Challenges we ran into None of us had ever used Kinoma hardware, AutoDesk Fusion 360, or had made a Bluetooth-enabled application. Accomplishments that we're proud of We are certainly proud of all we learned about the above tools. We're also very proud of the functionality and aesthetic of StarKey. What we learned We learned how to make Kinoma Create applications, how to use AutoDesk Fusion 360, how to make a Bluetooth-enabled app, and how to use pulse width modulation on servos. What's next for StarKey We'd like to improve the housing to be more robust. We'd also like to see how my parents would use it in their house and add functionality based on their user feedback. <div

projects.title: Weight Assisted Linear Kinetic System (WALKS)
projects.tagline: WALKS is a linear generator that utilizes the weight of the user to push a magnetic piston within a wrapped coil. This could be implemented in high-trafficked walkways/highways to generate energy.
projects.description: Inspiration Initially we wanted to focus on areas of untapped energy generation that were abundant and consistent. Our immediate thought turned towards children's playgrounds, specifically turning all of the mechanical equipment into mini generators. We quickly realized this was not feasible and frankly unsafe for the children. Then, while walking down Bruin Walk we noticed the quantity and consistency of people utilizing the path. We realized there was a potential to harness additional energy through this consistency by implementing a generator within our walkways. What it does WALKS is a linear generator which uses a weighted piston system and induction to generate energy when pressure is applied. When the piston is pressed, a row of magnets pass through a coil of conductive thread wrapped around the casing, generating an alternating current. Springs within the casing allow the piston to return to its original position after pressure is released. The alternating current is then passed through a diode bridge rectifier to convert the current to DC and store it within a capacitor. How we built it We began with a proof of concept using a conductive thread wrapped around a plastic container and manually moving magnets to test whether or not a current was generated. Once successful, our team split into 2, with one half working on the electronics and the other half working on the hardware. To design the casing we used SolidWorks and after multiple iterations, settled on a final d…

projects.title: Arduino Sign Language (ASL)
projects.description:
Ever wanted to be able to convert someone signing in ASL to
characters. With Arduino Sign Language, you can!
This project allows for people who do not understand American Sign Language themselves
to read what someone who is signing is trying to say. The project consists of a glove with
multiple sensors on it to detect the different positions of the hand along with the movement
that it is doing. Flex resistors were attached to each finger and could sense how curled
the finger is. An IMU (gyroscope/accelerometer) was connected to the top of the palm
to detect movement. The data was collected for each letter into a CSV file then fed into
a TensorFlow neural net as training. The model was exported after training then it was
used to predict the new data from the sensors when actually using the project. The model
was able to achieve around 90% accuracy in validation data.

projects.description: Autolab Labs Autonomous end to end 2D materials discovery from exfoliation to characterization, no human in the loop. Built at TreeHacks 2026. What It Does AI Materials Researcher is a multi agent platform that autonomously executes the entire 2D materials research pipeline. Describe an experiment in plain English the system plans it, controls the hardware, detects flakes, runs spectroscopy, searches literature, and generates a full report. The platform connects three layers: 1. Custom hardware A graphene stamping/straining jig with stepper motors controlled by a Raspberry Pi running a local VLM. The researcher talks to the jig through natural language prompts. 2. Intelligent vision A two stage CV + Claude Vision hybrid pipeline for real time flake detection. Local computer vision optimizes contrast and finds candidates in ~30ms, then Claude Sonnet 4 verifies and classifies each one in ~3 seconds. 3. Autonomous agents An orchestrator agent coordinates synthesis, characterization, and theory sub agents. When the jig finishes exfoliating, it signals the platform to begin the next step automatically. Raman spectra are analyzed, peaks are fitted, and results are compared to literature all without human intervention. Project Structure How It Works 1. projects.title: Braille18
projects.description:
A modular text-to-braille display specially designed for children learning braille. It uses character recognition and a solenoid array to immediately go from a page of text to a tactile braille display that is large and easily readable by little fingers!
"The aim of this project was a cheap text-to-braille display, compared to the more expensive displays common on the market, aimed at children who don't have the fine motor control to effectively read most commercial displays.
It uses OCR to scan and parse a page of text into a string, then converts it into display-sized chunks and translates to braille. This braille is then outputed to the display mechanism.
The display consists of an array of solenoids, arranged in blocks of braille characters. The blocks are entirely modular - each can be hooked directly onto the end of the last block, snapping into place mechanically and linking to the next one. Electrically, the modular nature is achieved by having data outputed on a serial line so each block only needs to be connected to the previous one.
The project is partially functional - all the components work, but the very high power draw of the solenoid array means it heats up extremely quickly, so can not be run for long periods of time without the risk of burning something out, and any attempts to limit current mean the large number of solenoids don't have enough power to run."

If you cannot make friends during 0 week or have goldfish memory when it come to putting names to faces, use Chatfish to make ends meet.
"""Chatfish"" is an innovative project for new students, using a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, camera, and microphone for facial recognition and interaction. It aims to ease social awkwardness by remembering faces and names, and facilitating engaging conversations in the initial school week. Key concepts include facial recognition, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, text-to-text, and language models. Our team efficiently integrated these concepts during the build week, optimizing algorithms and fine-tuning systems for Chatfish to generate engaging responses.

projects.title: Doornamo
projects.tagline: Doornamo is a generator that converts the mechanical energy of opening a door into electric energy which can be stored, providing an easy source of clean energy for office buildings, schools, etc
projects.description: Doornimo aims to utilize the every day actions of human beings (such as opening and closing a door) to produce energy. Its set up includes a motor anchored to a door frame as well as a wheel against the ground. The wheel spins the motor's spindle, producing a voltage potential difference between the motor's pins. These pins are connected to a rectifier circuit so that Doornimo generates a positive voltage both opening and closing the door. Once rectified, the voltage is then used to charge a capacitor and store the generated energy. We built this project through the use of 3D-printing as well as bread-boarding for the electronics. We were challenged by the mechanics of this design. It was difficult to integrate different aspects of our design into one functioning object. Despite the challenges, we're proud to have made a stable proof of concept, capturing waveforms of the energy Doornamo has generated. Future iterations of Doornamo would include a more simplistic design, reducing the wheel count from three to one. We would also want to look into ways to improve Doornamo's efficiency, to produce more substantial amounts of energy. <div

projects.title: Matless DDR
projects.description:
We engineered a matless version of Dance Dance Revolution with
two play options: one featuring a center-mounted LIDAR and the
other utilizing a set of arcade buttons.
The primary objective of our project was to create a more accessible version of arcade
games like Dance Dance Revolution. We aimed to eliminate the need for space-inefficient
arcade machines, enabling people to enjoy Dance Dance Revolution without making a
purchase. To achieve a ’matless’ experience, we incorporated a 360-degree rotating LIDAR
sensor. This sensor captures the player’s foot movement, interpreting their location as
input for the game.
In addition to the LIDAR sensor, we implemented an alternative play option using arcade
buttons. Utilizing arcade buttons from Adafruit, this second play option includes buttons
that light up upon presses, with each press interpreted as input to the game. This dual-play
approach also allows for a two-player mode. We employed a Raspberry Pi 4 (RPI4) to
manage both the arcade buttons and the LIDAR sensor, collecting data seamlessly.
For the game interface, we utilized an open-source Dance Dance Revolution (DDR) platform,
enhancing the play experience by implementing additional song options. The RPI4 served
as the central hub for collecting data from both the arcade buttons and the LIDAR sensor,
ensuring smooth integration and operation.

projects.title: Modular Mobile Robot
projects.description:
Build a simple multipurpose mobile robot
Programming mobile robots is a whole field inside robotics. To even start exploring algorithms like trajectory generation, though, one must have a robot to work with. The goal of this project is to build such a mobile robot so that it is possible to experiment with real algorithms on a physical, easy-to-build robot.
There are two parts to this project. The first involves building the actual robot. We plan on using a Raspberry Pi platform that controls a four-wheeled drive system, based on the Sand Flea robot from Boston Dynamics. Perception of this robot will be based on the Intel RealSense R200. The second part revolves around writing an API that allows a user to control the robot easily without having to worry about inner workings of the robot, like PWM control of the motors or reading encoder values. We would also like to incorporate ROS into this robot.
We also plan on documenting the process of building and programming this robot extensively, so that anyone can make their own modular mobile robot.

projects.title: Mozartonomy
projects.description:
This piano is a box of memories. It records what you play, stores its data, and plays it back with the exact key movements, tempo, and pitch - allowing you to keep it forever.
As big classical music fans, we both always wondered how composers like Chopin or Liszt used to play the piano. However, because we were born in different lifetimes, we never had the opportunity to watch them play. Thus, Mozartonomy's piano records everything that a pianist plays and allows us to store it in a file. This is then played back so that we can see the exact movements that the pianist executed on the piano. This is a masterpiece that can be kept for life, and for others to still be able to see in the future. Our piano consists of 12 keys (1 octave). Using buttons below each key, it senses what the user plays and records the time the buttons were pressed, as well as the times that the buttons were rest. All these data are stored into a file and played back. It is played back using 12 solenoids which drives each key, allowing the user to look at how those keys were individually pressed and how they were played. The sound of the piano was driven by a speaker. We also enclosed the piano in a nice little box that was laser cut. It has record, play, and stop buttons which allows the user to intuitively perform these actions. Our hope is to eventually scale this up to a full, 88-key working piano. :)

The code is written for the Sparkfun ESP32 Thing board, and programmed using the Arduino IDE. It initializes two sensors, a CCS811 Air Quality Sensor and a Sparkfun Sonar Sensor breakout board. After initializing the sensors, a simple server is created on port 80 on the WiFi, and hosts a website locally. The website displays the data being transmitted from the sensors in real time. If the detected distance from the sensors to the pipe surface becomes too large, it indicates an integrity violation in the surface of the pipe.

projects.title: Sheer Highlight Attack
projects.description:
Mecanum wheel reconnaissance drone used to follow reflective vest wearing individual with depth detection avoidance.
The purpose of this project was originally to create a two wheel recon drone that could detect objects and follow a person around unhindered. We then changed our design to be a four wheel mecanum robot which would allow for more space in the center for components and side to side movement and drifting capabilities. Our design then changed again when one of our encoders was broken so instead of a motor controller/ROS system, we switched to using a FeatherWing and just the Jetson Nano. Our robot uses an algorithm to detect someone wearing a bright fluorescent vest by first masking an image based off of a lower/higher threshold of some highlight color, then gray scaling it, then running cv2 contours to grab what remains and get the maximum size in a bounding box and then adjust for the height and width of the target. Overall there were many design changes and tribulations we had to overcome, resulting in almost every night late in Techspark and Robo Club, but even if it doesn't do all its intended goals perfectly, we, as a team, are very proud of what we created.

projects.title: USB C Tube Amp
projects.tagline: It's a vacuum tube headphone amp that runs off a USB Type C connection.
projects.description: Inspiration USB Type C can deliver more electrical power than the older USB standards. It should be enough to run a vacuum tube amplifier. What it does You plug it into a USB port and you plug your headphones into it. You play your music. It combines the vintage warmth of tube audio with the modern convenience of USB Type C. How I built it I soldered electrical components together starting from a USB C breakout board. The vacuum tube circuit runs off 12v, so a buck-boost module was used to increase the USB supply voltage of 5v to 12v. A cheap digital-to-analog converter was also attached to the breakout, supplying an analog signal to the tube circuit. The actual tube circuit was based on this . It uses a low voltage 12AU7 dual triode vacuum tube and two IRF610 MOSFETS operating as a Class A amplifier. Challenges I ran into Initially, the tube amp had the interesting property of picking up AM radio signals. Faint music would be played even when no signal was sent through USB. This was solved by placing a resistor between the tube's plate and the input capacitor. Accomplishments that I'm proud of It works. What I learned I gained a lot of experience working with analog circuits. I learned wiring techniques such as avoiding ground loops to obtain a good quality audio output. I also learned that my earbuds were reversed in polarity. The one labeled for the left ear actually receives the right ear's signal. This solved a lot of mysterious "issues" of a polarity reversal somewhere…

projects.title: Zip
projects.description:
a different kind of cable-driven robot.
Set it on a table, hook up a few cables, and let it go.
An entirely self-contained cable driven robot. Instead of having a big frame with motors at all the corners, I am going to put all the motors onto the center end-effector. An INVERSED cable driven robot! Zip will have all the ropes bundled up in its center; to set it up in a new environment, just pull those cables out and mount them to the edges of a table. My robot will only move on a flat surface (unlike the example pictures provided).
The mechanism has opportunities to be elegant beyond its portability. The cable winches will be mounted with encoders, so manually pulling the cables to the table edges during setup will automatically calibrate Zip to whatever surface size you choose.
It will definitely run slow in this first iteration, but my priority during the hackathon is to get precise and smooth motion down while having it be entirely self-contained. A secondary goal is to make it physically robust and and portable; to be specific, make the calibration and setup process smooth.
The biggest challenges I anticipate include the mechanical design to fit everything in a stable configuration in such a limited space, and to keep all the cables in tension as it moves. There are fantastic resources online for traditional cable-driven robot assemblies that I will take advantage of.

projects.description: treehacks2017 "hotDog project" for treehacks2017 Inspiration During sweltering summer days, cars can be become very hot very fast. Many people accidentally leave their dogs, or even young children and infants, in their vehicles, while picking up groceries or shopping. Even though they expect to be gone for only 20 minutes or less, during this time, car temperatures can reach about 110 degrees within minutes. We wanted to prevent this problem and stop these tragic and preventable deaths from happening. What it does Hot Dog is an IoT application, using IBM Watson's Node RED and the Raspberry Pi. Users place the hardware, comprised of the Raspberry Pi and a temperature sensor, near their windshield in the car. Hot Dog will keep track of the temperature within their vehicle while they are running errands. When the measured temperature is about to reach dangerously high levels, the application will send a text message to the user, warning them that they are potentially putting their pet/child at risk of heat stroke. If the car does become extremely hot, the app will also send a call to Animal Control or 911 automatically as a second resort. As another addition to the IoT capability, we have a twitter account linked as well that tweets from the pet's perspective calling for help on a large social scale. Two motors made up a flywheel that darts could be pushed into, and the pushing was meant to be done using a solenoid and a metal pin but during build week the solenoid fell apart. projects.description:
Confounded by electrical circuits? New to graph theory? > Need help with homework? The best method to learn is to write / draw it ourselves. But for complex topics we might not get the proper intuition by just looking at a static picture. This is where our project comes in! We will convert hand drawn electrical circuits into a schematic by performing optical character recognition (with our model). A simulation is then run for the schematic to solve it and give a better intuition of the underlying concepts.
ECE major ? Take a hand drawn circuit, convert it into a schematic and simulate it.
CS major ? Take a hand drawn graph, find the MST, DFS, BFS, etc. and visualize it step by step.
This can be a great learning aid to students who might not have access to other proprietary tools and help professionals make quick and dirty simulations The project can be extended as an AR application.

The Thrill of Board Games Combined with Robotic Precision
We will bring the wonder of robotics to the board game industry with Infinifun. The general gameplay is similar to that of Pong, in which a ball collides with walls and scores points when it reaches the end of the board. However, our game ball will be a robotic disc with infrared sensors to detect the end of the table and bounce off the edges, emulating a physical wall. As such, the game can be played on any flat surface, such as your dining room table at home, and is extremely portable.
Unlike Pong, the players do not have paddles, but place colored tiles on their side of the game board that adjust ball movement. A green tile speeds up the ball, a red tile slows down the ball, a blue tile offsets the ball direction by a certain amount, etc. The ball contains a color sensor that determines when to adjust its motion. Each player wants to arrange his/her tiles in such a manner to direct the ball towards the opponent’s goal.
Welcome to the board game of the 21st century!

projects.description:
A box that jiggles. It also play music.
Purpose: to make playing music a more engaging experience by the inclusion of ferrofluid that dances to your favorite songs.

Box internally lined with LEDs, with the names of all builders engraved on the top-side opening of the box. projects.title: Little Dipper
projects.description:
Personalized colored candles!
Remember that ombre candle you saw through the window of Yankee candles? Perhaps you didn’t like the color scheme, or wanted something more than a generic, store bought candle. Well, look no further! The Little Dipper brings to Build18 2018 our very own, customizable candle designer! You pick and choose the colors you want your candle to be, and watch as the Little Dipper creates a custom candle right before you.
The Little Dipper consists of a rotating disk containing heated plates. Each plate contains molten wax of different colors. Alongside these hot plates is a tub of water. In the center of the rotating disk contains a robotic arm mechanism. The setup also contains a graphical interface on a laptop. The user can select their preference of colors and the order they want these colors to appear in, and then press a “Send to Dipper” button.
When this button is pressed, the Little Dipper picks up a candle (provided!) and alternates between dipping it into the molten colored wax and the water. Once the coloring is done, the Little Dipper places the candle into a separate area from which the user can pick it up.
Enjoy your personalized ombre candle!

projects.title: Pomo-do-your-work
projects.tagline: A response to the apparent and prominent reliance on technology and a return to physical games and longer attention spans. We bring to you pomo-do-your-work, a mechanical timer to help you focus.
projects.description: We recognized that our heavy use of technology has resulted in difficulties with maintaining attention and discipline when it comes to work. To combat this, we developed the "pomo-do-your-work" device, a mechanical contraption that helps users efficiently complete their tasks and regain their discipline. The device utilizes gears and rotational blocks to divide 30 minutes into intervals of 1 second, 10 seconds, 1 minute, and 10 minutes. Users work for 25 minutes and then take a break, using this time to play one of our specially designed thinking games for 5 minutes. This repetition not only improves focus and problem-solving skills, but also makes the task more enjoyable by having something to look forward to. Our main challenge was getting the stepper motor to provide enough power to turn the gears, but we found a semi-fix by using rotational blocks that can be turned by hand. Our next steps include implementing a working motor system, adding a sound system during breaks, and developing more games for users to play during their 5-minute breaks. <div

By detecting a user's emotional state (arousal and valence), the system modulates a shared AR environment and provides physical haptic feedback to a second user, allowing them to "feel" the first person's internal emotional volatility. The Science: Affective Computing The core logic relies on the Circumplex Model of Affect, which maps human emotion onto two axes: 1. Key Features Biometric Fusion Engine: A custom Python bridge fuses hardware data (GSR spikes) with software inference (Gemini audio/visual analysis) using a weighted algorithm (0.75 Hardware / 0.25 AI) to determine the true "intensity" of the emotion. projects.title: Real Subway Surfers
projects.description:
Real-life Subway Surfers where you become the character! Hop on
the board and enjoy the game!
The purpose is for users to experience a more challenging Subway Surfers. Instead of playing it on computer with a keyboard or on the phone, players can control the characters by stepping on a board. This is a fun way exercise while also playing games. We used acrylic for the top of the board to get an aesthetic look with a wooden base where we connected all the electrical components. For each piece, we used metal strips sandwiched around foam. When the user steps on a specific wooden board, the top metal strip bends to touch the bottom strip. The top metal bars are connected to ground, so when the top connects with the bottom metal bar, the bottom bar is grounded, thus sending a signal to
the Arduino which determines what key should be pressed. After many hours of debugging, we overcame hardware issues, such as poor wire connections from the solder and copper tapes, and software issues, where the Arduino wouldn’t stop running the same section of code. Now, the final product is ready to play!

projects.description: SkyBox SkyBox is a compact and low cost solution to gathering local air quality data. On a local scale, air quality can greatly differ within a community, leading to negligence of areas with low air quality. What it does SkyBox uses a P2.5 Dust Sensor and an Air Quality Sensor to measure, record, and transmit accurate data of the levels of particulate matter and various gasses in the immediate air to map out the air quality of local areas. This data is mapped with GPS location and used to generate an overlay on an interactive map that one can use to analyze air quality on a local scale just by checking a website. How it works The SkyBox hardware is built on a custom designed 3D printed chassis that holds an Arduino Uno wired up to a P2.5 Dust sensor and an Air Quality sensor. The chassis was designed in Fusion 360 and can be mounted to anything from busses, to delivery vans, to drones. The SkyBox software is a combination of Arduino and Python scripts. The Arduino code interfaces with the SkyBox to record sensor data and send it over the serial port, where it is parsed with a Python script that writes the data to a csv file and then uses the Maps API to generate the Air Quality Map. The same data is used to create the interactive public Air Quality Map as well. Generated Map

projects.title: Tonal Paintbrush
projects.description:
Paint sounds in 3D space. Listen to your painting by moving the brush around your painting
There are 2 main components to this project: the desktop component (a computer connected to a Kinect and a set of speakers), and the handheld component (a paintbrush containing a WiFi transceiver, an MCU and a small circuit). The Kinect is used to track the user's hands, and the computer is used to operate the Kinect and produce sounds.
Setup:
The user holds the paintbrush in their right hand. The paintbrush has a small MCU, a WiFi transceiver and a small circuit containing a button and a potentiometer. The Kinect will face the user, tracking the position of their right hand.
When the user presses the button on the paintbrush, the transceiver communicates this to the computer (communication protocol TBA), and the current position of the paintbrush is recorded by the computer. The computer also produces a sound.
Now when the paintbrush is placed in the vicinity of the recorded position, the computer plays back the sound (allowing the user to explore their painting).

projects.title: Virtual Meadow
projects.description:
Using VR, CV, and real life objects to create an immersive nature experience in a contained space.
Allow users to feel like they are engaging with a beautiful natural environment, using VR to place them in the space and real "props" such as grass and a stream to make the experience feel real, even when on campus.
The physical space consists of a small (6'x6') square of grass, with a running "stream" shaped into the square and some objects a user can pick up - a dowel, stones, a 'plant', etc.
The virtual space is similar to the physical one, but provides a more environmental experience with immersive sound and visuals. The dowel, rocks, & stream correspond to a stick, rocks, and a river in the virtual world, and the user can engage with each of these items. A Kinect tracks the current depth map of the environment - allowing us to have an accurate idea of where our interactive items are. Depending on the technology available to us, we will use either the Kinect or a Hillcrest sensor to track a user's hand and use of the objects.

projects.title: Water smarter
projects.tagline: Water Smarter, an adaptive automated garden watering system | Treehacks 2021 Submission
projects.description: Water Smarter Giving plants the right amount of water is not only good for the plant but good for the planet. Our project aims to create an adaptive automated watering system using soil moisture sensors and valves. Inspiration Inspired by SIU Carbondale's Green Roof, we wanted to create an automated garden watering system that would help address issues ranging from food deserts to lack of agricultural space to storm water runoff. What it does This hardware solution takes in moisture data from soil and determines whether or not the plant needs to be watered. If the soil's moisture is too low, the valve will dispense water and will send a message via Twilio to notify the user that their plant has been watered. How we built it First, we tested the sensor and determined the boundaries between dry, damp, and wet based on the sensor's output values. Then, we took the boundaries and divided them by percentage soil moisture. Specifically, the sensor that measures the conductivity of the material around it, so water being the most conductive had the highest values and air being the least conductive had the lowest. Soil would fall in the middle and the ranges in moisture were defined by the pure air and pure water boundaries. From there, we visualized the hardware set up with the sensor connected to an Arduino UNO microcontroller connected to a Raspberry Pi 4 controlling a solenoid valve that releases water when the soil moisture meter is less than 40% wet.

projects.title: 【Eudaimonia】 ：Ai伴学引擎与真人guider指导相结合的未来教育——以Favor群聊机器人的PBL项目开发为例
projects.tagline: Eudaimonia 是一套AI 陪伴引导，真人作为guider的教育引擎系统，取名自亚里士多德"活出完满潜能"之意，通过打破学科边界、建立跨学科思维、以 PBL 带学生走进真实世界，让每个孩子探知自我、发掘潜能，把成长从偶然的幸运变成结构性的必然。
projects.description:
Eudaimonia 是一套开源教育引擎系统。名字取自亚里士多德的核心概念——人发觉自身潜能、活出完满状态。

它想解决的是一种教育遗憾：许多本有天分的孩子，因为缺少一位引导者（guider），在统一化的筛选机制中被磨损，最终偏离了心中的热爱。产品的使命，是通过软件与服务尽可能降低门槛，让"探知自我、发掘潜能"从少数人的偶然幸运，变成一件结构性、可复制的事。

技术上，它摒弃传统独立建站模式，采用"一引擎多皮肤、校验闸闭环"架构，把教学经验拆解为标准化、可校验、可复用的知识原子，运行时结合学科配置与学生实时状态，动态渲染专属学习空间。产品以应试学科为入口，以自我认知与人格成长为出口，搭载具备独立人格的 AI 智者作陪伴引导——定位为"思考助产士"而非答案工具。整套体系 不靠专利筑墙，而以真人guider的链接，标准质量与社区公信力构建长期护城河，让优质个性化教育规模化落地。

教育哲学落在三点：打破学科边界、在 AI 辅助下自由而有陪伴地探索；建立跨学科素养与思维结构；以 PBL 做中学，带学生走进真实世界——例如队进入 AdventureX 等黑客松现场，从发现问题、用户调研到 vibe coding 开发，最终做出真实产品（如互助机器人 Favor 帮帮），完成从纸面到实践的闭环。

projects.title: ARI
projects.description:
ARI, your mental health companion.
In a situation of high stress and frustration, people often forget to breathe, which can lead to an anxiety or panic attack. A gentle reminder to focus on the feelings of their body can help people relax and find peace in their mind. Currently, phone apps like Headspace and Calm provide mental health support passively. Users have to become aware of their symptom first before choosing to use these apps to address their discomfort. These apps do not provide real-time mitigation and relief, and are therefore only effective during the aftermath.
Ari presents a proactive solution that assists the users before they experience anxiety attack. Ari is a lamp with awareness. It blends in with the ambient environment by silently listens to a user’s heart rate and level of activeness. Ari interacts with the user with its breathing light that effectively occupies user’s peripheral attention and guides the user to match their breathing pattern with Ari.

projects.title: Crowd Density Monitoring Vehicle
projects.description:
Tethered drone for persistent aerial monitoring of crowd density
A tethered drone with a long cable connected to a ground station which processes on-board data and returns meaningful information on crowd movements and patterns.
We chose to use tethered drones for their ease of maintenance, deployability, and increased airtime. This makes them useful for persistent monitoring of crowd density for long events, such as music festivals or campaign rallies, without needing to disturb the crowd or take the system offline.
We will use a computer vision algorithm that gets a reference of the empty space before an event starts, and compares it to live video of the event space to find the distribution of the crowd, processing it onboard and relaying it down to the ground station to convert to a heat map, which can be used to help prevent overcrowding and its associated dangers.

projects.title: Flywheel energy storage prototype
projects.description:
How to make a better battery
We wish to create a prototype for a flywheel energy storage system. Instead of storing electricity chemically like conventional batteries, these systems store energy mechanically. This is accomplished through spinning rotors at high speeds.
There are two types of flywheels - direct drive flywheels and magnetic flywheels. Direct drive flywheels use mechanical contact to store and extract energy from the rotor. Magnetic flywheels use magnetic bearings and electrical motors/generators to access energy without friction. These flywheels tend to be stored in vacuum sealed containers to further reduce friction.
We would like to experiment with rotor shape to test efficiency. We are also interested in learning how to efficiently create a vacuum enclosure. Another interesting variable to experiment on is the torque generated, and how to control the torque with rotor shapes and gymbal setups.

The possible future of interaction between human and humanoid robots.
We are going to build a simple robot arm which is controlled by hand and arm gestures. Basically, the robot arm follows the gestures of one's hands and arms. It is a different way of human-machine interaction. Its application is vast: precision manufacturing, surgery, wearable robots (such as exo suits), etc.
General methodology: 1) get data of hand or arm motions with flex sensors attached to hand and arm; 2) process the data with RPi; 3) send data to the receiver of the robot arm and perform corresponding actions.

Our invention will drive users to get off their chairs and experience the outdoors more. We implement two circuits, one that stays on the user's workstation and one that they wear like a wristwatch. When the user has been sitting for too long, a high-pitched buzzer sounds to incentivize the user to go outside. When the user has been outside for long enough, as determined by the outside light intensity, a light on the wristwatch will turn on. The user can hold the light to the circuit with the buzzer to turn the buzzer off. <div

projects.title: HexDisplay
projects.description:
What if display but hexagon?
The project aimed to create a LED hex display, capable of displaying real-time information such as the current time, weather, and bus schedule. The display consists of hexagons, each representing a component of the information to be shown. It was created by designing a PCB in KiCad and soldering WS2812 strips onto it. We then screwed it onto acrylic with headers connecting the boards. A Pi Pico W was used to control the display with an I2C bus for peripherals such as a light senosr. Tkinter was used to generate masks, which were used to define the shape and arrangement of LEDs within each hexagon. The Picos were programmed using the C SDK and CMake. We were able to build a functional LED hex display that only displayed preset masks. We hope to expand the software further in the future.

projects.title: Hogwarts Duel Tournaments
projects.description:
Harry Potter fantasies come to life through the synergistic combination of both hardware and software.
Our proposed project draws inspiration from the Harry Potter magic system, simulating the characters’ wand magic through the intersection of hardware and software in a packaged magic dueling game. Using computer vision techniques, a laptop’s built-in webcam will detect wand motion created by the user, and based on this particular movement pattern, will display the corresponding spell on the laptop screen and trigger the user's wand to emit the appropriate color for the spell used. These spells will translate into attacks against the current NPC the user is battling within the game. This mingling of hardware and software creates a dynamic and engaging user experience, deepening the player’s immersion into the game’s simulated Harry Potter universe.

projects.title: LED Matrix
projects.description:
LED board that you can play with to make a light show.
# Hardware
- 1 64x96 LED board driven by a Raspberry Pi, purchased from Adafruit.
- 1 leap motion
- FPGA from the ECE labs
- 1 web-capable touch screen device (like a phone!)
# Software
- We want to build a web app that lets you select a song from Spotify or YouTube, and then select what effects you'd like from a menu.
- The Raspberry Pi listens to the network for these updates, then downloads the song and starts playing it, potentially using the FPGA for rendering complicated 3D image transforms.  We also want to be able to have effects synced live to BPM and maybe try to figure out where in the song we DROP THE BASS.
- The Leap Motion provides input to the RPi, so you can tap the air and add additional effects.

projects.title: Rob (Self-Driving RC Car)
projects.description:
Car drives itself through an Arduino, ultrasonic sensor, and an algorithm to avoid objects and drive through obstacles.
We disassembled the RC controller that came with the car, wired our Arduino into it, and sent commands through the Arduino to thereby control the car. Originally, we had planned to use a Jetson Nano, but since we encountered power supply issues with the Jetson, we decided to switch to an Arduino. Since we moved from Jetson Nano to Arduino, we also moved from camera to ultrasonic sensor since the Arduino has much, much less computing power. We also encountered issues with the LiDAR sensor, which we wouldn't be able to use with an Arduino anyways.

projects.title: RoboCurry
projects.description:
A ping pong ball launcher that's the best beer pong player in the world!
RoboCurry is a 1-foot tall semiautonomous launcher that uses computer vision and mathematical computations to locate the target Dixie cups and accurately throw ping pong balls into them. After receiving the location of the cups from a Raspberry Pi, an Arduino will in response adjust the launcher's horizontal angle, angle of elevation, and launching power. These factors will be set by a servomotor, a rack and pinion, and a pneumatic air pump system respectively. When ready, it will shoot out 1 ping pong ball in storage like a cannon. We plan to optimize its movements to make it incredibly speedy and precise. See "Photos" for a general depiction of the size and components necessary for RoboCurry.

projects.title: Robotic Bartender

Are you missing your favorite mixed drinks but completely lost on how to make them? We have the perfect robot for you!
We are building a bartending robot. This robot will mix different quantities of liquids by using a pulley system and a stepper motor to move a cup between the suspended bottles. We will also incoporate a frother to mix the final drink. An iOS app will be designed to interface with an Aduino which will allow you to select the drink that you want to be made for you.

projects.title: Rubot
projects.description:
A Rubik's cube solver. Place the cube into the machine and watch it solve it.
We wanted to get an introduction to a project involving electronics. The parts for the solver were 3D printed and assembled, we made a PCB board and we made a solving algorithm. The cube solver works by placing the cube on a tray which rotates, and a head that holds the cube in place and flicks upwards to rotate the cube. Both servos are controlled by a raspberry pi. The algorithm follows steps people can use to solve Rubik's cubes (specifically from https://rubiks-cube-solver.com/how-to-solve/) rather than a known cube solving algorithm. Eventually we ran into issues with connecting the raspberry pi to the CMU Wifi, so the solver is not functional.

projects.title: Service Rover
projects.description:
A bot to help people navigate and explore spaces
Basically, the idea is to create a simple rover coupled with obstacle sensors and a mobile app that provides haptic (and visual) feedback to help people navigate complicated spaces. We're designing this for situations where service dogs aren't viable (spaces where they aren't allowed or spaces where they just don't work well) and generally small spaces. At the very least, we're building a mobile webcam- something that, for example, can go around a room and explore it on command to allow someone else to explore the space vicariously (or navigate it).
Implementation: first Arduino/RPi, Omniwheels, hc-sr04's, mobile app; then add cameras, figure out exploration algorithms, more sensors.
Team: rmehndir, vrramesh, vrbahl, parunapu

projects.title: Spaceteam
projects.description:
A physical hardware hot-pluggable version of the popular mobile game Spaceteam.
This is a 3-player hardware implementation of the cooperative multiplayer mobile game Spaceteam (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaceteam). Each player has a console with 3 dial, button, or switch controls and a screen that displays commands. The players must work together to keep up with the commands and set the controls to the correct settings. This project will also allow the controls to be hot plugged and rearranged dynamically between games. Each control will be mounted on a prototype board and have an LCD that displays the control's name and current value, the control itself (a button, toggle switch, or potentiometer), and an ATtiny84. The controls will fit in to a larger console with an LCD that displays instructions. All controls will communicate with a master Arduino Uno over an i2c bus to allow for dynamic reconfiguration of the game layout.

projects.title: Supercapacitor Smartphone
projects.description:
Charging your iPhone to 100% in under 1 minute
Scientists have been claiming for years that advances in technology will result in supercapacitors in our phones, which would let your smartphone charge almost instantaneously. However, they never actually do it!
I'm here to construct an iPhone that runs off a supercapacitor with comparable energy to the lithium battery that they currently use. This involves the charging mount and the modification of an actual iPhone to run off a supercap, which has a voltage range of 0-2.8V instead of a LiPo's usual 4.2-3.6V.
I have an old iPhone 6s, which has a 6.55Wh battery. To charge that in a minute takes (6.55Wh*60mins/1hr) = 393 Watts for 1 minute. Since the supercaps peak around 2.7-3V, this will draw >100 amps from my power source! Tons of power! I'm using either several 2S lipos in parallel or a high power DC source I have.
iPhone modification is easy, or at least the phone battery repair youtube channels make it look that way.

projects.title: The Ultimate Defroster
projects.description:
Center of your frozen pizza still cold after heating it into the microwave? Never again.
By placing an infrared camera in a microwave, one can display a heat map of its contents. In so doing, users can determine (based on colors) the temperature their food is at, thereby eliminating any guesswork on whether their food is cooked!
This can be achieved by mounting an IR camera on the microwave, taking IR pictures every second or so. This data would be parsed by a wirelessly connected Raspberry Pi, which would display the temperature content on an LED matrix mounted on the front of the microwave. By lighting up selected LEDs at different colors, the LED matrix would effectively display a 2D heat map of the contents of the microwave.

projects.title: Wake Up!
projects.description:
We want to make a head-mounted product that vibrates whenever the user is detected with low attention level. For instance, if a person is falling asleep while driving, it will detect the user’s brain wave and recognize that the attention level is relatively low, thus will start vibrating and wake the user up. The same functionality can be helpful to students who really wants to pay attention in class.
To achieve this goal, we will only need a head-mounted brain wave sensor, some small vibration motors, and a microcontroller. The logic is pretty simple: first use the brain wave sensor to collect data when people are focusing or distracted; then create a machine learning model to train an algorithm to react when the user is distracted; finally connecting the sensor and vibration motor to the microcontroller and add a button that could turn it on and off.

projects.title: 物理书签:让你的创作空间拥有 Ctrl + Z
projects.tagline: 由 dimOS 驱动的双具身空间记忆系统，让机器狗和机械臂记住物品在哪里，并像 Ctrl + Z 一样整理和恢复你的物理空间。
projects.description:
「物理书签」是一套由 dimOS 驱动的双具身空间记忆系统，由 Unitree Go2 机器狗、Galaxea A1Z 机械臂与 ASUS Ascent GX10 本地计算平台共同组成。

系统通过共享的空间语义记忆，理解“什么物品在哪里、应该被送到哪里”。机器狗负责全局空间感知、巡逻、定位与运输，固定在工作台上的机械臂负责局部物品抓取、分类和归位。

当创作者结束工作后，系统可以识别散落的工具与材料，通过机械臂完成拾取，再由机器狗运输至指定收纳区域；当用户重新开始创作时，系统还可以依据保存的空间状态，恢复熟悉的工作区布局。

它不仅清理空间，更为现实世界保存一个可以随时恢复的“物理书签”。

当前原型重点验证了 dimOS 对机器狗导航、空间感知、设备控制及双机器人协同任务的编排能力，并以固定物品抓取和跨空间运输作为核心演示闭环。

projects.title: Analytical Engine
projects.description: Our goal is to emulate a working computer inspired by the Analytical Engine proposed by Charles Babbage in 1837 on an FPGA. This would include implementing the Engine’s key architecture - the mill (analogous to an ALU), the store (memory), the reader (input), and the printer (output) - with a design that incorporates elements faithful to Babbage’s initial ideation and writings translated by Ada Lovelace, while taking necessary “shortcuts” through the FPGA platform for the sake of feasibility. On the physical side, we plan to build a custom punch card reader and an output “display” with a thermal printer module as a nod to the Engine’s original design. We will start small, and aim to implement basic computer functionalities (basic arithmetic operations, registers, etc.) before moving on to expanding those features and building the physical aspects of the machine.

projects.title: BuildGCC
projects.description: The goal of this project is to build a better GameCube Controller (GCC). The GCC, which came out over two decades ago, is still commonly used around the world to play Super Smash Brothers. However, there are many issues with the controller's design that lead to inconsistent inputs, which can be very frustrating for competitive play. A recent project called PhobGCC has explored the use of custom hardware and software to improve the reliability of the controller. This Build18 project will attempt to build upon the PhobGCC's design, exploring the use of Hall effect sensors and Kalman filtering to improve the controller's performance. And hopefully, more folks at CMU will learn a bit about Smash, too!

projects.description: Our project is to design a vending machine that encourages people to exercise. The vending machine will allow you to select a drink/food item, then require you to do some exercise proportional to the amount of calories in the item you chose. It will use CV to detect some basic exercises, like burpees or jumping jacks. Only after completing the exercises will the item be dispensed.  The user will pay the vending machine using Venmo and select an item, and the vending machine will then determine the number of calories the user needs and dispense the product as the user performs their exercises. The motivation behind is sometimes people feel guilty of eating vending machine food due to high calories. This vending machine makes users do exercises to consume the calories, and at the same time our user can have some fun doing exercises.

projects.title: Eyes on the Road
projects.description:
Eyes on the Road is your second set of eyes on the road for your electric scooter. No more looking back to see approaching cars, no more drivers turning you into a road pancake!
Eyes on the Road implements a 60GHz radar to detect objects behind the scooter, returning the distance to the object with precise millimeter measurements. The distance is relayed to a small display on the handlebars, and when the distance crosses a certain threshold, the scooter lights up with warning LEDs and displays a message on the display. On the handlebars, there are two buttons that controls the turn signal LEDs present on the scooter. The display, buttons, radar, and LED lights communicate with each other using the I2C protocol.

projects.title: FPGA CNN Accelerator
projects.description:
Accelerate neural net on FPGA
We implemented a basic hand-writing recognition neural net with C that includes basic matrix operations such as add and multiply. We got the model to run on the embedded ARM core on the FPGA while implemented the operations with SystemVerilog. Then we experimented the interface between the CPU and the FPGA and tried to replace the matrix operations with hardware implementation to speed up the calculations. Eventually everything works on simulation, but due to the limiting logic and memory capacity of our FPGA, we weren't able to fully synthesize everything.

projects.title: Lazy Laundry
projects.description:
For all the lazy people that are not lazy enough to stand infront of the laundry machine.
Our device is a laundry machine monitor that uses a vibration sensor and an Arduino. The output of the vibration sensor is processed by the Arduino and converted a digital voltage. When the voltage is 0, it indicates no vibration, which means the laundry machine is "OFF". Conversely, when there is some voltage reading, it indicates "ON". This result is sent to an LCD display through the I2C bus and it will display "Processing..." when "ON" and "Ready!" when "OFF". We attempted to use Zigbee wireless communication protocol to send the ON/OFF information wirelessly but we were not able to.

projects.title: "Magic" Card Shuffler
projects.description:
Hack the card shuffler to give the exact deck you want!
By connecting RFID tags to each card in a standard 52 deck of cards and building an electronic card shuffler with an RFID reader, our system will be able to deal the cards in the pairings/orderings the user wants. The user can use an app to control the deck he wants to receive from the shuffler or the cards he wants to deal to the other players.

projects.title: 3D Scanner
projects.description: We intend to build a cost-efficient 3D scanner that takes images of small objects and reconstructs them in 3D. The main physical components consist of a bottom plate to place the object and to help correct the camera, a small car with camera to move around to preset locations. The software component involves primarily the algorithm to reconstruct the 3D object from the 2D images

projects.title: 4 Wheels Robot
projects.description:
Virtually connected single wheel robots in a set of four. Let's see what can be empowered by teamwork of wheels.
virtually connected single wheel robots in a set of four. Will it be able to handle delivery, assist with moving, or carry you on a Segway mode and show you around our campus? Let's see what can be empowered by a teamwork of wheels.

projects.title: A Buggy Time
projects.description:
Want to push objects up hills and time yourself doing it? We got you covered.
Push practice happens late in the night and often it is a battle against the elements. At times there are mistakes made in timing and this could be detrimental to the team when choosing or training their pushers. This project aims to leverage existing RFID/IR technology that is used in marathons and apply it to timing pushers.

projects.title: Air Horn Orchestra
projects.description:
Like fine arrangements of music?  Want to bring them into the world for EVERYONE to hear?  We've got you covered.
Step one:  gather MIDI file of the world's finest compositions
Step two:  gather a LARGE quantity of air horns
Step three:  adjust horns to emit various musical notes, all of which are beautiful
Step four:  attach all air horns to servos connected to a micro-controller
Step five:  convert MIDI files into servo instructions
Step six:  bless the air with the choir of the gods
Step seven:  profit

projects.title: AlexaX
projects.description:
Alexa will follow you like a hungry, sad pupper.
Technology today is constantly playing catch-up with today's fast-moving, relentless consumers. With limitations on budget and time, people often cannot afford more than one smart home device. Introducing AlexaX, an innovative, on-the-go smart home solution that will follow its user to the ends of the world, as long as there is WiFi.

projects.title: Animation Game
projects.description:
Live animation using wands!
There's a "stage" area visible by two webcams, one from the front and one from the side. Each person has a wand at the end of which is a colored LED. The 3D location of the wands is detected live using computer vision analyzing the webcam footage. Each wand is mapped to a body part: for example, one player could control the left foot, one the right foot, and the third player could control the head. Together, you can bring the character to life!

projects.title: AutoMailman - An Aerial Payload Delivery System
projects.description:
Our solution to the last mile delivery problem - autonomous drones that deliver a package right to your door.
We plan on building a small conceptual demo of what would be part of a larger autonomous delivery system. We will mount a computer vision system and package pickup claw to a standard drone in order to pickup and dropoff packages. Our system will be able to locate a colored packaged within a room, create a path to it, pick it up, and fly to another location with the package in hand - all completely autonomously.

projects.title: Autonomous Underwater Vehicle
projects.description:
Glide and explore below the surface without ever getting wet
We aim to design and manufacture an autonomous vehicle that will effectively navigate through submarine environments. It will be equipped with a camera and a ultrasonic sensor array, allowing autonomous navigation and object identification.

projects.title: Backpack Charger
projects.description:
Imagine never having to worry about finding the nearest outlet!
Since students are always carrying their backpacks and always in need of outlets to charge their electronic devices, our plan is to design a backpack charger. This backpack will have built in chargers that use a gyroscope or kinetic energy (of students walking to or from class) in order to supply power.

projects.title: Bagel Maker
projects.tagline: Bagels from the future
projects.description: Inspiration What it does How I built it Challenges I ran into Accomplishments that I'm proud of What I learned What's next for Bagel Maker . <div

projects.title: BeverageBot
projects.description:
The ultimate couch potato tool... as long as you refill it occasionally
BeverageBot is an automated localized drink delivery system that utilizes embedded systems, computer vision, and deep learning in order to optimize your drink enjoyment. It's basically the _____ of _______. (Insert more buzzwords here)

projects.title: Bluetooth Bike Computer
projects.description:
A bike computer that is affordable AND connects to your phone
Bike computers are either expensive and connected, or they're cheap and don't connect to anything. With just a few sensors and a Bluetooth-enabled microcontroller, we're going to let you track your biking without breaking the bank

projects.title: Board Writer
projects.description:
Making professors handwriting legible
We propose to build a system to write on white boards/ chalk boards without the need for human intervention. The system will essentially consist of two gliders, to horizontal and one vertical that can grasp a marker or a piece of chalk. The system then writes on the board as if being played as a movie. The notes/ content can either be scanned via a camera or entered via a pdf.

projects.title: Build a Bot
projects.description:
Quickly test and build robot with modular parts.
Our project is to make testing designs much easier by having a modular design for parts all with a single connector. Each part should be able to know what parts it is connected to and will figure out if the other parts are defective. So each part will act independently.

projects.title: Build sk18
projects.description:
This skateboard lights up differently depending on how hard you kick and push.
This skateboard lights up differently depending on how hard you kick and push. Using a microprocessor to interface with an accelerometer and led strips, the skateboard lights will be different depending on how fast you speed up and slow down. Long exposure photos of a skate session will be taken at night to achieve light painting with the skateboard.

projects.title: Can You Sit With Us?
projects.description:
System of sensors that monitor room occupancy from any location
We will use small pressure sensors placed on the seats in the target area, which don’t intrude on the privacy of the occupants. These units will communicate with a central hub, which will then send its data to an online database. There will be a web interface that pulls from the database to display live room occupancy information.

projects.title: Chess Moves for Itself
projects.description: We are building a chess board where a human plays against an AI. While the human physically moves their chess pieces like in a typical game of chess, the AI moves the pieces without any human intervention — each piece is moved via an electromagnet attached to a gantry. A low-power circuit underneath the board keeps track of which pieces are where, including tracking the human’s moves. “Chess Moves for Itself”.

projects.title: DJ.io
projects.description:
Chess, Go, StarCraft... there's only one arena where humans still reign supreme, the final frontier: Doodle Jump.
We will make a system to attempt the world record on hit mobile game Doodle Jump. It will perform CV on the pixels from the screen to detect platforms, make decisions about where to move and shoot, and tilt an iPhone with a motor to perform the movements.

projects.title: Dum.py
projects.description:
Ever had to hold onto waster for longer than 10 minutes? Is it because you couldn't find a trash can? Enter the Dum.py
Our project is an autonomous trashcan that will eliminate the need for public trash bins and recycling bins. Using multiple cameras to implement SLAM, the Dum.py will have the functionality required to plan a path navigate sidewalks filled with pedestrians, cross streets, and even return to the appropriate facility to empty out waste.

projects.title: Dynamic Room Correction
projects.description:
Smart speakers that calibrates itself according to its surroundings, providing optimal audio regardless of its location.
Smart speakers that calibrates itself according to its surroundings, providing optimal audio regardless of its location. A microphone is used to measure the room's acoustic response and the DSP automatically compensates for acoustic imperfections. Similar to the technology in the Apple Homepod and Sonos' Trueplay.

projects.title: ECE Signage Board
projects.description:
Providing easily updatable signage in front of major ECE classrooms.
ECE does not have signage like in University Center or the Gates Building that provide information about events occurring in a given room. Therefore, ECE should develop its own signage system.  The system would be easy to configure, use, and update.  The system will display fields such as time, event name, speaker name, class number if applicable, additional comments.  The system will be wirelessly controllable. There will be a user interface that a user can add new events as needed and the system will display events as they occur.

projects.title: EPA Phone Home!
projects.description:
In developing world contexts, measure if water and air is safe using simple sensors with an iphone.
Developing countries are getting access to smart phones before they get access to clean water.  With low-power, low-cost sensors a smart phone can  take all the measurements needed to establish that a water sample or surrounding air is safe or dangerous.  I plan on reading the sensor data in, processing it in iOS, and communicating it to the user with the iPhone API.

projects.title: FPGA Rasterization
projects.description:
Triangle rasterization using Hardware with FPGA.
Video games use many triangles to represent the frame to be rendered. To accelerate this, we decided to design hardware that would be able to translate screen space triangles into pixel colors that show up on the monitor. We tried to print a case with the PLA, but the print failed.

projects.title: Grab Hand
projects.tagline: Using flex sensors and Arduino to model hand position on a 3D model of a hand in real time.

projects.title: Harry Potter VR Spell Dueler
projects.description:
A virtual reality spell dueler using Google cardboard.
Using **Google cardboard**, we will write a web application that manipulates reality using a smartphone's camera. We will draw over reality spells and their effects for players of the game. We hope to have an N player game, but will shoot for 2 for demoing. **All you should need to play this game is just your smartphone**, Google cardboard, and a wand of your own choosing!

projects.title: High Five Bot
projects.description: This is a 4 DOF robot arm that will detect an open palm, track it, and give it a high five. It will feature elements of Numerical Inverse Kinematics, Stereoscopic 3D Plotting and Computer Vision to ensure that the High Five Bot will be ready to tackle any number of high fives in any position smoothly.

projects.title: Intentional XR Locomotion
projects.tagline: An XR locomotion system using IMUs and BCI to enable movement via micro-gestures and intent, allowing full VR control while doing nothing but laying down—making boundless VR more accessible than ever.

projects.title: Internet Controlled Teleoperation Robot
projects.tagline: It is a TeleOperation Robot which can be controlled over the internet by anyone having the credentials.
